svg.title: Pocket Voice cloud architecture and data flow
svg.desc: The browser talks over HTTPS to one Python process in a GitHub Codespace. The process calls Groq for speech recognition and answers, speaks with PocketTTS on CPU using a locally saved voice profile, and stores metrics in SQLite. Model weights are downloaded once from Hugging Face.
svg.text: Pocket Voice: cloud architecture and data flow
Ask by voice or text, get the answer spoken in your own voice
GITHUB CODESPACE (cloud VM) · one Python process · private HTTPS port 8501
Mic audio (WAV) or typed text reaches the pipeline
Audio → Groq Whisper → text (skipped when typed)
Question + recent history → Groq chat → answer
Answer text → PocketTTS → speech in your voice
Text and audio are returned and played
One metrics row saved: no audio, no transcript
Your recording goes to PocketTTS (trimmed to 20 s)
Saved once as a profile, reused for every answer
psutil samples: live to the UI, to SQLite every 30 s
History charts are read from SQLite
Weights downloaded on first use, then cached
Sent to Groq: question audio or text, plus recent chat history.
Your voice recording and profile are not sent to Groq.
Web search on: fresh facts, search words leave
